question: How do you bind a ServiceAccount to a Pod so the Pod can access the Kubernetes API?
selection_rationale: SO answer score 18. ServiceAccount not covered in any existing fixture (coverage matrix shows all four types needed). 3-hop path (ServiceAccount→RoleBinding→ClusterRole) is fully annotatable from graph. New resource coverage with clean relationship type fit.

ground_truth.answer:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: my-sa
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: pod-reader
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: read-pods
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: my-sa
    namespace: default
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: pod-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api-pod
spec:
  serviceAccountName: my-sa
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: my-app:latest
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.ServiceAccount: provides an identity for processes that run in a Pod; automountServiceAccountToken controls token projection
io.k8s.api.core.v1.PodSpec: serviceAccountName field specifies which ServiceAccount the Pod uses for API access; defaults to "default" if not set
io.k8s.api.rbac.v1.RoleBinding: grants the permissions defined in a Role to subjects including ServiceAccounts within a namespace
